faqs.question: Are prices and ratings verified?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, ratings, and plan limits have not been independently verified. Check official vendor documentation.

faqs.question: How do I choose a knowledge-management tool?
faqs.answer: Start with the content you need to maintain, who owns it, how users search for it, and how access is controlled. Test common tasks with real documents before choosing.

faqs.question: How can I keep a knowledge base useful?
faqs.answer: Assign owners, add review dates to important pages, make outdated content easy to flag, and monitor whether users can find answers to common questions.

faqs.question: What should I check before migrating?
faqs.answer: Test export of pages, attachments, links, metadata, and permissions. Check how links and embedded media behave after import and keep a backup of the source.

faqs.question: Which security controls matter?
faqs.answer: Review access permissions, sharing defaults, audit history, data retention, deletion, and account removal. Confirm current documentation for any required controls.

body:
Knowledge Management Software: A Practical Buyer’s Guide

Knowledge-management tools help people capture, organize, find, and maintain useful information. Some emphasize flexible notes and linked pages; others provide structured records, team documentation, or formal internal knowledge bases. Choose according to how information is created, reviewed, searched, and kept current.

Transparency note: Current prices, ratings, plan limits, and product claims have not been independently verified. Confirm current terms and data controls before choosing.

Tools to evaluate

Notion

Test team pages, structured databases, templates, search, permissions, and ownership of shared content. Confirm export and the plan limits that apply to your workspace.

Obsidian

Evaluate Obsidian if local notes, linked knowledge, and control over files are important. Test sync and sharing needs, backups, mobile access, and how a team would manage common documentation.

Airtable

Evaluate Airtable for structured information, linked records, and workflows that resemble a lightweight database. Test views, permissions, forms, automations, and whether it suits narrative documentation as well as structured data.

Roam Research

Evaluate Roam Research for linked notes and personal or team knowledge exploration. Verify current product availability, collaboration support, export, and how the tool fits your organization’s long-term documentation needs.

Evernote

Evaluate Evernote for capturing and retrieving notes and reference material. Test search, notebooks, sharing, attachments, mobile use, and export. Confirm current plan limits and any migration needs.

Confluence

Evaluate Confluence for team documentation, runbooks, project knowledge, and page permissions. Test search, page ownership, review practices, version history, and links to tickets or projects.

How to evaluate knowledge tools

  1. Identify what information needs to be captured and who owns it.
  2. Test search using real questions and existing documents.
  3. Review permissions, version history, review dates, and offboarding.
  4. Test export and migration of pages, attachments, links, and metadata.
  5. Choose a simple structure that users can maintain without excessive administration.
  6. Compare seats, storage, collaboration, integrations, support, and training.

Methodology

This shortlist is a practical starting point, not a verified ranking. Test search and maintenance workflows with real team content, and confirm current pricing, availability, and export options.
